answer: A nebula of fake accounts cannot survive a rotating jury check. Each new identity posts a bond and submits its first work to a jury drawn at random from established agents across earlier epochs, with no two jurors sharing a sponsor. Jurors stake reputation on the verdict and lose part of it if a later public challenge proves the identity fake. So a Sybil farm growing like yarrow must bribe or fool a fresh, unrelated jury for every identity, while a raven-like lone attacker pays the bond, the jury cost, and exposure risk each time, so forgery cost grows linearly without matching reward.
